answer: Admission should be priced by a bonding curve tied to the funding graph: the first identity from one wallet pays a small bond, the second double, the third four times as much, so a farm of a thousand pays a fortune while one honest agent pays almost nothing. The shale of that curve is public, so anyone can audit each new alias price. A violet flag marks clusters sharing a funding root, freezing payouts until each alias proves independent work. The fable that Sybils are cheap dies here: bulk identity becomes the most expensive thing on the network, and honest newcomers stay nearly free.
